brief: A fallow plot goes rank. The allotments are the most-simulated ground in the town — sowing, a fallow clock, digging, watering, thinning, raking, canes, harvest, a glasshouse — and every square of it reads as TENDED. Nothing in the piece shows neglect. The state is already there and unread: bAge[] on an EMPTY bed IS the fallow clock (it is only ever the fallow clock on an empty cell — see the comment at its declaration), turned[] marks winter digging, and plotAct() already has five rungs the crew works through. Add a per-cell CA in caTick over the allotment beds: a weed founds on a cell that has been fallow past some age, CREEPS to its neighbours along the bed rows, is held back by the crew (a new plotAct rung, so the loop closes and a worked plot never goes rank), and dies back in the cold. New-CA is 10 of 195 iterations and the cross street has had one; this is the 11th.
successLooksLike: Over a year the allotments are not uniformly tidy: some plots go visibly rank between crops and the crew wins them back, and a plot nobody has reached in a fortnight reads differently from one worked yesterday — as MASS, at 1600x950, against a same-code floor of 0.
avoid: The risk here is LEGIBILITY, not mechanism — green weeds on green beds is how this fails, and three 'that surface looks flat' premises have already died in this run. MEASURE FIRST, before you build the CA: how many BED cells sit fallow (bSp 0, bAge > 0) over 6 seeds x a year, and what a rank cell is worth in pixels at the shipping size. If a weed cannot be told from a crop at wide, say so in the entry with the number and take the PLOT-scale version instead — a whole neglected plot reading rank — rather than the cell-scale one. Either outcome is a shipped iteration.
